summary: Stochastic RSI: a stochastic of the 14-bar RSI, with smoothed %K and %D lines and levels at 80 and 20.
overview: The Stochastic RSI applies the stochastic formula to RSI instead of price. It moves between 0 and 100 in its own pane, faster than RSI, with a blue %K, an orange %D and a zone between 80 and 20.
It shows where RSI sits in its own recent range.
how: First RSI(close, 14). Then raw = (RSI - lowest RSI of 14 bars) / (highest RSI - lowest RSI) x 100. %K = 3-bar SMA of raw. %D = 3-bar SMA of %K.
Because it measures RSI against itself, it often reaches 0 or 100.
use: Some traders watch moves above 80 or below 20 as short-term extremes.
Use %K crossing %D as a quick momentum signal.
Pair it with a trend filter so you read it in context.
Watch for it leaving an extreme zone.
alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
It is very sensitive and gives many signals.
